vehicles.title: 1912 Marsh Metz
description: Motorcycle manufacturer Marsh, later Marsh Metz, only existed from 1900 through 1913, and today it is not quite a household name among riders. This is a shame, because its high-quality offerings form a key part of the history of motorcycling in America, with many important firsts to the company’s credit. In fact, founder Charles Metz is said to be one of the very first to use the term “motor cycle,” which was used to advertise his relatively primitive, engine-powered Orient motorcycle—generally acknowledged as America’s first production motorcycle—in 1898.

Metz’s earliest experiments with motorization had involved a rather improbable-looking hybrid: an engine-and pedal-powered tandem bike used, somewhat ironically, for training and pacing riders for the Orient bicycle racing team!

Metz joined forces with fellow constructor A.R. Marsh in 1905. Marsh brought his own innovations to the deal; his single-cylinder motorcycles were among the earliest to use more durable, purpose-built frames, rather than adapting existing bicycle frames. He also employed the engine as a stressed member, positioned directly below the seat. The joint Marsh Metz firm continued to offer a single-cylinder motorcycle, but also added a two-cylinder model to the catalogue.

Displacing 1,087 cubic centimeters and powering the rear wheel via belt drive and only one speed, this V-twin engine was rated at up to 10 horsepower—about all that one would want, considering the single band brake on the rear. Importantly, it did so more smoothly than the shallower-angle V-twins produced by other manufacturers at the time. It also led to the bike’s unique appearance: The engine was once again used as a stressed member, tying the frame together at three points. Though the bike is full of eye-catching details, including the cigar-shaped polished fuel tank, it is the distinctive 90-degree motor and the unique frame design that wonderfully showcase the engine as the true “heart” of the machine.

One of few surviving examples, this Marsh Metz was acquired by noted collector Otis Chandler in 2002, and it was restored by Antique Motorcycle Works of Oregon City, Oregon, the following year. It was acquired by Sam and Emily Mann in 2006 following Chandler’s passing, and it has remained in their collection on static display ever since.

Rare, significant, and quite attractive to boot, this 1912 Marsh Metz beautifully illustrates a moment when motorcycles were no longer merely crudely adapted bicycles, and were well on their way to becoming elegant, brilliantly engineered two-wheeled steeds in their own right. The stunning restoration still appears fresh as the day it was completed.

vehicles.title: 1921 Ford Model T “Bonneville Taxi”
description: 1921 Ford Model T “Bonneville Taxi” Custom Built By Darrell Zipp of Zipper Motors as fun transportation to and from Bonneville Salt Flats to the hotels in Wendover during Speed Week. Looks like a stocker but as you get closer you can see all of the modifications Darrell made to make it easy to drive so that he or his wife Rosalee could enjoy it.

Running gear was sourced from a 1970’s Nova with 4 cylinder engine, th350 3 speed automatic transmission, and a 10 bolt differential with drum brakes. The front suspension was upgraded with custom handmade aluminum tapered 4 bar and vega steering box with cross steer. The rear has a ladder bar and buggy spring. The drum brakes are operated by a Wilwood brake Master cylinder under the floor. The original steering column throttle was converted to a gear shifter. 12 volt system with Alternator, stereo, and CB radio.

Full Custom wood bed and tailgate all handmade. Marvins Creations built the tufted seat, Under the seat is a custom aluminum fuel tank. All 5 wheels are extremely rare 1920’s racing knock offs by “Houck.” You may never see another set. Cruises at any speed comfortably, but I’ve never had it past 55. Very cool car built by one of the best fabricators in the business.

vehicles.title: 1932 Ford BLOWN Original Henry Steel 3 window Coupe
description: 1932 Ford 3 window coupe. Original Hotrod and real Henry Ford Steel body. We don’t have early history on the car but its been a Hot Rod for a very long time. The last owners had the car for over 25 years.

The last cosmetic work was performed in the 1970’s when it was painted Dark red Metallic with Gold velour interior. Very nice chop was performed sometime before that, its at least had 4” removed and looks killer with the angled A pillars. It has a smoothed cowl, roof insert, and frenched antenna. (the vent tray is still intact under cowl) All the garnish moulding are originals that were chopped to fit. Doors and decklid fit nice.

Chassis is a modified original with dropped front tube axle and adjustable 4 bar suspension. Rear is a GM 12 Bolt with transverse leaf spring and Ladder Bars. Engine was built about 15 yeas ago by previous owners who were avid drag racers. Built for street use, it runs amazing on pump gas, starts easy, and is super crisp when you hit the throttle…ts Rarin to go!! Built with an early 70’s 350, BDS 671 Blower, Pro Form carbs, electronic ignition, Edelbrock finned aluminum Carbs, and shorty headers with full stainless exhaust. Backed by a th350 automatic with shift kit. Disc brakes up front with drum in back.

Interior is a mix of the 70s velour interior with upgraded 1965 mustang buckets and black vinyl door panels. Sun gauges adorn the roadster dash with a SW Tach on the column drop. Windshield still flips out. Trunk is finished out from the 70’s in velour.
Lots of Patina all over, this baby has been around! Real deal Hot rod that is lots of fun to drive, turns heads wherever it goes. Don’t buy that plastic junk, own a real Hot Rod!

vehicles.title: 1932 Ford Roadster V12 Jaguar Pro Touring
1941 Ford Pickup “Charlie”
description: 1941 Ford Pickup “Charlie.” Tucson car since new and was the shop truck for “Charlies Auto Service.” previously located at 228 E 6th st here in Tucson. (Now Crooked Tooth Brewing Co. ((If you look close you can still see the old Charlies signage on the Building.)) The shop closed when Charlie died in the early 80’s. The Truck was stored in that building until I rescued it in 2013 from Charlies son Robert. At that time we rebuilt the brakes, fuel system, and installed new tires. The current paint job was done in 1948. The hand lettering was done by “Spencer,” who was well known for hand painting the Barnum Bailey Signs according to Robert. Loaded with era accessories and even a flame thrower exhaust!
Amazing piece of Tucson History! Not For Sale

vehicles.title: 1946 Ford Coupe Blown H&H Flathead
description: 1946 Ford Business coupe built from the ground up with no expense spared. This 46 was purchased in 1951 by the previous owners grandfather who left the car to his son in the 1970’s who decided to undertake a full build with his son around 2010. This car remained with the same family for over 70 years!

Built by professional shops in Texas , Ornduff Hot Rods, and Bruces Rod Shop with receipts totaling over $170,000. The S.C.O.T. Blown flathead was built by H&H Flathead in Crescentia, CA. The car was finished around 2011 and still has less than 1000 miles on the build.

Extensive metalwork was performed on the car to assure excellent fitment and laser straight body panels. Headlights were frenched, bear claw latches installed, and firewall smoothed and recessed for the Wilwood brake booster. Finished in its original color of “Dynamic Maroon,” fully sanded and buffed to a show quality mirror finish. Underbody is painted body color over “Lizard Skin” sound deadener.

The interior utilizes a “Glide” adjustable bench seat, 6 hides of “SpinneyBack” hand dyed leather in the color of “Telluride” Beautifully restored Dashboard with a combination of NOS gauges and Stewart warner gauges including a column mounted tach and 40 Ford Deluxe steering wheel. Note the hand made stainless clutch and brake pedals and Skull shifter knob on the T5 manual transmission.

Powered by a H&H Flathead built 59A flathead stroked to 284 cu in. with SCAT rotating assembly dynamically balanced, ported, polished, and relieved. Topped with Offenhauser heads, a S.C.O.T. Blower, and dual Stromburg 97 carbs. Fitted with MSD electronic ignition and the coolest set of hand made headers and exhaust I’ve seen in awhile. If you are not familiar with H&H, look them up, they are the best in the business. Backed by a T5 5 speed manual with overdrive and a Ford 9” differential with 3.50 gear. Rear suspension was upgraded to a parallel leaf and front has a Pete and Jakes dropped axle, split wishbones, spring, and Vega cross steer with power disc brakes.

Certainly one of the finest 46 ford street rods available today. Built by 7 generation owners who cared and the end result has a truly timeless style, packed with the best components and materials available.

vehicles.title: 1954 Hillegass Sprint Car
description: 1954 Hillegass Sprint Chassis# JE-54-19

Hiram Hillegass began building race cars in 1919 while working at Mack in Allentown, Pennsylvania. By the time he died in 1960 at the age of 65, he was recognized as one of the foremost builders of single-seat race cars in the Únited States, a stature that was endorsed when he was elected to the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 1997.

#19 was built in 1954 for Dixon Sawin and raced successfully in the URC until 1972. Purchased from the Sawin estate in 1992, it was restored in 1994, It may be the most original, unmolested, early tube frame-torsion bar suspended Hillegass in existence. GM V8 powered with Hilborn Fuel injection, a vertex Magneto, and a CAE in/out Box. Very historically significant, #19 still retains its original speed equipment including its Halibrand Quick Change Differential, Halibrand Disc Brakes with outboard brake lever, Halibrand Magnesium Knock Off Rims with period Firestone racing tires, Hillegass torsion bar suspension and tube axle. The Leather upholstery and grille cover are all original, as is over 80% of the stunningly hand crafted aluminum body panels.

The fact that #19 survives in such an original unmolested condition is remarkable. Dan Owens, in his noted book “Vintage and Historic Indianapolis race cars” described the sprints of the 50’s and 60’s as the “meanest, most difficult to drive, most overpowered and exciting cars in oval track history.” There are very few original examples remaining.
Has not been started in a number of years so it will need some attention to be fired once again.

vehicles.title: 1956 Oldsmobile 88 w/ 28k original miles
description: This 1956 Oldsmobile Super 88 Holiday coupe has just 28,854 original miles and is perhaps one of the nicest low mileage Super 88’s available anywhere, backed by a complete and documented ownership history
Arguably the most handsome car to come out of the GM design studios since the war, this Oldsmobile Super 88 is a brilliant study in 1950s style and engineering.

The car remained completely unrestored until 1991 when Harold Badger purchased the car with only 25,720 miles on the clock and remaining 100% in original condition. He commissioned a complete repaint in its original colors of Turquoise and Ivory paint scheme. All the exterior trim was removed and refinished to show quality. The engine and transmission were removed and resealed and painted. The engine compartment was detailed with factory paint quality stamps intact.
The end result was good enough to have won the Ransom E. Olds award at a National Oldsmobile Club meet as well as being selected to the Oldsmobile 100th Anniversary parade in Lansing, Michigan.

The interior is 100% original in every way, and shows you what a well-preserved machine this really is. Seats, door panels, carpets, and even the headliner are factory-installed pieces that remain in show-ready condition. There’s some wear, but it’s hard to believe this car is 80 years old. The dash is a spectacular showcase for Oldsmobile’s jet-age styling, with a pair matching of oval-shaped panels in front of the driver and passenger, joined by a stainless grille that houses the radio. The bench seat is still firm and comfortable, and there have been more than a handful of passengers in the back during this car’s long life—it’s just too nice. Everything works as it should, including the radio and heater, and the steering wheel shows no signs of aging or stress cracks, just a warm patina. In the trunk you’ll find the original fabric and what very well might be the original spare that has never been down.

Powered by its original 324 V8 engine backed by a 3-speed Jet-A- Way automatic transmission, which, like the engine, has been removed and resealed, but never rebuilt. The chassis is rust-free, thanks to dealer-applied undercoating that has been touched up here and there, but never completely removed. The suspension is completely original and rides in a way that no restored car could ever equal. Power drum brakes stop the car with confidence, and it wears 7.60×15 whitewall tires that are period correct

Documentation is extensive, including a paper trail back to the original owner, Myrtle Forward, who owned the car until 1977. 2nd owner Henry Koenig cared for the car from 1977 until 1991. The Third owner, sympathetic restorer, and collector of truly low mileage original cars Harold Badger kept the car until around 2016 when it was sold to the previous owner who sold to me just recently. He bought the car with 28,031 miles and there is a stack of mechanical receipts showing repairs and associated mileage that accompany the car that now has a mere 28,854 miles on it. There are also volumes of 1956 Oldsmobile promotional materials, copies of original titles, an original registration from 1960 in Myrtle Forwards name, and newspaper articles from the 1990’s showing Harold Badger the third owner of the car.

Combining the low mileage with sympathetic restoration work, this is like driving a new 1956 Oldsmobile off the showroom floor. With extensive documentation that verifies the low mileage claims, this car is an excellent candidate for preservation class judging.

vehicles.title: 1963 Ford Falcon Futura 260 V8
description: 1963 Ford Falcon Futura 4 door sedan. Restored by a Falcon Club member and enthusiast in it very rare original specifications. Factory 260 V8 car with automatic transmission and originally sold new in Dallas Texas.

Solid rust free car that retains all of its original, floors, trunk, and rockers. No evidence of any body panel replacement, everything fits very well. It was professionally repainted in its original color of “Tucson Yellow”, code “R” with a white 2 tone insert. All of the chrome and stainless is in very good shape. All weatherstripping is in good shape and all glass is very nice and functions with ease.

The car retains its original 260 V8, very rare in a falcon. With the v8 came 5 lug big brakes all around, this car was upgraded with Mustang 4 piston disc brakes and dual master cylinder for added safety. The factory automatic transmission shifts great. Chrome American racing 15″ wheels make it look great and rides nice with the radial 225 50 R15 Kumho Ecstas. A heavy duty 3 core aluminum radiator and flex fan were installed recently, car cools great.

The interior was completely redone to a very high standard in white with beige cloth seat inserts and beige carpet. A modern stereo was added in the glove box with Kick panel speakers and even a subwoofer system in trunk with amplifier. All seals and weatherstrips are in good shape.
Well sorted Falcon ready to enjoy! Make it your daily driver or car show cruiser!

vehicles.title: 1966 Corvette 427 Coupe
description: 1966 Corvette coupe L36 390hp Big Block. True Survivor car that retains most of its original sunfire yellow paint and has just over 66,000 miles believed to be correct. Many years ago the front surround and passenger door were repainted due to a very minor ding in the passenger side fender above the bonding strip. Im assuming they painted the whole surround because of rock chips perhaps. The Paint still shows very nice but is lacquer cracking on the nose. There are also quite a few other small flaws, chips, etc in the paint due to being applied over 50 years ago. Excellent door and hood gaps. Interior is original with the exception of the carpet and seat covers which were replaced. Beautiful Dash and gauges. Seat belts are still soft and retain the original tags. Has original Jack with hammer. Matching numbers drivetrain. Optioned with TI ignition, teak wheel, telescopic column, power antenna, 3.55 Posi rear diff, and Knock off wheels. All 5 wheels are original Kelsey Hayes, not reproduction. All glass including windshield are original to the car and never removed, all in very good condition. All chrome is original and still shows very nice. No rust on frame. You would be hard pressed to find a nicer original Big Block Vette anywhere. Just got judged for the first time and was 50 points away from a Top Flight, so with a few minor changes it will easily get the blue ribbon. Excellent Candidate for a Bloomington survivor award.

vehicles.title: 1972 Bronco
description: 1972 Bronco, original Paint 41k miles. One owner Bronco from Pocatello Idaho until 2017 when it was sold to the second owner who lives here in Tucson. He had it consigned at a local dealer who I purchased the car from. One of only 792 produced in “Calypso Coral” paint code. The paint is all original with the exception of the passenger front fender that had a repaint back in the 70’s. Still shines beautifully but does have nicks, dents, chips, and scratches from its 60 years of existence. 41,000 miles believed to be original but not noted on title.

All original Drivetrain that has only been serviced and resealed as needed. Recently I upgraded the front drum brakes to a Wilwood 6 piston Disc brake with power assist. I was able to utilize the original hubs. I upgraded the suspension with a “wild Horses” 2-1/2″ lift kit. Very nice progressive springs that ride ultra smooth. I installed Bilstein Shocks on all 4 corners and added US Mag 5 slots with 30x 9.5 15 BFG All Terrains. Great stance. Transmission is the original 3 on the tree manual. Differentials are factory 4.11 gear.

The interior was originally white but needed replacement. Seats were redone in Black with houndstooth inserts. The floors were fully insulated and covered in custom fitted German Square weave carpet. I added a Retrosound stereo that has bluetooth with Mic for phone calls with Infiniti speakers. there are also two USB plug ins. An all new Vintage air AC and heat unit was installed that makes driving in the summer much nicer.
Its nearly impossible to find a Bronco in such original unmolested condition. Ive kept the original Brakes, springs, heater box etc just in case anyone wanted to bring her back to stock.

vehicles.title: 1973 Lincoln Town Coupe w/ 25k Miles
description: 1973 Lincoln Town coupe with only 25,047 miles since new. Optioned as a Premium town coupe and factory ordered in code 1c “Raven Black” and GA code Black Leather.

This car had an Show quality repaint in its original color of Raven Black with a very high level of detail. Door jambs are as nice as the exterior and the car was fully sanded and Buffed to a mirror finish. All door, hood, and trunk gaps are excellent. The undercarriage retains all of its original floors, rockers, and trunk and reflect the condition of a true low mile vehicle.

All exterior chrome and brightwork are in excellent condition. Windshield was replaced with a new one sourced from AGP, all other glass is original and in very good condition. The Vinyl top is original and in excellent condition minus one scratch on the Driver side C Pillar (pictured) The hide away headlight work great. All exterior lighting works.

The interior was completely redone in high grade Leather and appears like new. Some custom touches were added like the two tone with camel Brown and Black, hand embroidered Lincoln Logos on seats and door panels. Very Well done. Power seats work great, AC blows cold, heat works, wipers work, AM FM stereo works as well. Power door locks function as intended and it has a trunk release in the glove box. Power windows all work great. All of the weatherstripping and seals are in very good condition. Trunk has been completely refinished and comes with a set of floormats. It has a supoer cool cup holder in forward console, the doors flip open when you turn the knob forward, glove box door opens when you turn the other way. The dashboard has no crack and is in amazing condition. Door panels are beautiful.

Powered by a 460 V8 and C-6 automatic that at a minimum were removed from the car and resealed/ painted. Runs and drives amazing and the 460 just purrs. AC has been upgraded to R134a refrigerant. The under hood is fully detailed to show quality standards. The car is optioned with power steering and Power disc Brakes.

Rolls On fully polished Factory Lincoln 15” aluminum Rims and Michelin Radials. I have seen a few of these era Lincolns but NEVER one restored to this level. True collector grade quality and you will certainly not find one nicer at any price.

vehicles.title: 1983 Don Yenko IMSA Camaro
description: Don Yenko, Jerry Thompson, and Chris Thompson, had been competing in the IMSA Camel GT and American Challenge series since the late 1970’s, in both Chevrolet Novas and Camaros. For 1983, IMSA changed their rules to allow cars to be built around a tube chassis. Dillon Race Works, out of Indiana, whose main business had been building tube frame cars for stock car racing, was selected to build this car. This was the first of several road race cars that Dillon would build. A similar Dillon built Camaro, driven by Gene Felton, dominated the IMSA “GTO” class in 1983 and 1984.

This car was raced at numerous tracks across the U.S., including Daytona, Sebring, Lime Rock Mid-Ohio, Sears Point, and Road Atlanta. In May of 1983, Don Yenko and Jerry Thomspson finished 3rd in a Kelly American Challenge race at Lime Rock.

In an interview with Jerry, he was quoted as saying “this was a very good race car, capable of winning, but Don and I did not have the financial backing as did Gene Felton and others. Back then, $10,000 was worth 30 horsepower, which was the difference between winning and losing“.

In 1983, this car was state of the art, with it’s tube chassis, dry sump oil system, rack and pinion steering and quick change rear end. With IMSA having no rules on engine size, just that cars must weigh 10 pounds per cubic inch, the car ran both a V6 and a V8, depending on the length of the track. Except for the engine and transmission, the car retains most of it’s original parts, as it has been in storage in California since 1987. Ironically, the car was purchased from Gene Felton, who raced a similar car and competed against the #11 Camaro numerous times. This was the last car Don Yenko competitively raced.
Sold on Bill of Sale
The last car to be competitively raced by Don Yenko
Built by Dillon Race Works
Raced at Daytona, Sebring, Lime Rock, Mid Ohio, Sears, Point and Road Atlanta
2nd Place at Pocono, 1983
Don Yenko and Jerry Thompson finished 3rd at Kelly America Challenge at Lime Rock, 1983
Tube chassis

vehicles.title: 1995 Corvette Indianapolis 500 Pace Car Edition
description: Always Garaged: This car has been stored in a climate-controlled garage under a premium car cover, entirely shielded from weather, UV rays, and moisture.

Exterior: The factory two-tone Dark Purple Metallic and Arctic White paint shines like new. The original, bold Indy 500 door graphics and red accent pinstripes remain perfectly intact and crisp with no fading or cracking. There are a couple small flaws that I’ve taken close up pics of in the gallery.

Interior: The unique black leather sport seats with vibrant purple inserts are in pristine condition with virtually no bolster wear. The headrests feature the beautifully embroidered official Indy 500 logos.
Top: The original white vinyl soft top is in good shape, operates smoothly, and seals very well as an original should.
Engine: Numbers-matching 5.7L LT1 V8 producing 300 horsepower. It starts immediately, runs flawlessly, and sounds exactly as it did leaving the showroom floor.
Transmission: 4-speed automatic transmission with the factory-ordered 3.07 performance rear axle ratio.
Wheels/Tires: Iconic 17-inch silver-painted 5-spoke aluminum wheels.
Options: Fully loaded with the mandatory Preferred Equipment Group, including electronic climate control, dual power seats, and the premium Delco/Bose stereo system.
Clean accident free Carfax, original owner’s manuals, selling Dealer plate, and original keys included.
New Michelin Pilot Sport tires were installed less than 30 miles ago in 6/ 2023,
